name: Proxmox_VE_Backups
description: Backup jobs, the guests each one covers, each guest's last backup and failed backups, and the guests no backup job covers.
technicalNotes:
BatchScript. One instance per guest per backup job, grouped by job (the job's comment, or its id when it has none), plus one instance per guest that no job covers, in the group "No backup job". A guest in two jobs has an instance under each. Needs only the PVEAuditor role.

The last backup and failures come from the logs of vzdump backup runs, read newest first; reading stops once every job guest has a successful backup, normally after the newest run. Backup files on a storage are not used: Proxmox lists them only to a token that may also create and restore backups, and hides them from a read-only one.

Calls per run: /cluster/backup, one included_volumes call per job, /cluster/backup-info/not-backed-up, one task-list call per online node, and one log read per backup run read (normally one). Nothing grows with the number of guests. At most the newest 50 runs are read, so a guest whose last good backup is older than that reads as having none.

LastBackupAgeHours ships without a threshold: the right value depends on how often each job runs, so set it per job group, for example > 26 on a daily job. LastBackupSizeGB is the archive size the run logged; Proxmox Backup Server runs log none, so it stays empty there.

FailedSinceLastBackup is 1 when a run newer than the guest's last good backup, to the same storage, names the guest as failed. A run that fails before reaching any guest names none; LastBackupAgeHours catches that case once it passes its threshold. Each failure's reason is in the backup run's entry in the source node's Task History in the Proxmox web interface. If any online node's backup runs cannot be read, these three datapoints stay empty rather than guess.

IncludedVolumes and ExcludedVolumes count the guest's volumes the job backs up and leaves out; the instance properties auto.pve_backup_included_volumes and auto.pve_backup_excluded_volumes name them, the excluded ones with Proxmox's reason ("not a volume" for a bind mount). A bind mount is never in a Proxmox backup, so ExcludedVolumes ships without a threshold.

NotCovered ships without a threshold: guests are often left out of backups on purpose. Set > 0 on the "No backup job" group where every guest must be covered.

datapoints.name: NotCovered
datapoints.description: 1 for a guest that no backup job covers, 0 for a guest in a job. Ships without a threshold; see technical notes.

datapoints.name: JobEnabled
datapoints.description: 1 when the backup job is enabled.

datapoints.name: IncludedVolumes
datapoints.description: Volumes of this guest that the job backs up. Their names are in the instance property auto.pve_backup_included_volumes.

datapoints.name: ExcludedVolumes
datapoints.description: Volumes of this guest that the job leaves out, such as bind mounts or disks set to backup=no. Their names and the reason are in auto.pve_backup_excluded_volumes. Ships without a threshold; see technical notes.

datapoints.name: HoursUntilNextRun
datapoints.description: Hours until the job's next scheduled run. Empty when Proxmox reports no next run, such as for a disabled job.

datapoints.name: LastBackupAgeHours
datapoints.description: Hours since the guest's newest successful backup to the job's storage. Empty when none is found in the newest 50 runs.

datapoints.name: LastBackupSizeGB
datapoints.description: Archive size of the guest's newest successful backup, in GB, as the run logged it. Empty for Proxmox Backup Server.

datapoints.name: FailedSinceLastBackup
datapoints.description: 1 when a backup of this guest has failed since its newest good backup. The reason is in the backup run's entry in the source node's Task History in the Proxmox web interface.
datapoints.alertBody:
A backup of ##INSTANCE## has failed since its last good backup, so the newest copy available to restore is older than the job's schedule promises. The failure reason is in the Proxmox task log for the backup run.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.
